before.statement: Here algebraic numbers means the REAL set A={x in R : sum_{k=0}^d iota_Z(a_k)x^k=0 for some d in N and integer coefficient list a_0,...,a_d with a_d !=0}, where iota_Z is Z -> Q -> R. A is countably infinite in ZF. An injection A -> N is specified by the least code of an integer coefficient list having x as a root, paired with the rank of x in its finite increasing real-root list. All embedded rationals lie in A, and RA is uncountable. No claim about algebraic closure or complex algebraic numbers is made: the available ambient field is R.
before.strategy: Reuse the explicitly specified surjection z:N->Z in ex-explicit-enumeration-of-the-rationals and the published J:N^2->N. Decode each n uniquely as J(d,t_0). For k=0,...,d decode t_k=J(u_k,t_{k+1}) and put a_k=z(u_k); evaluate the embedded-real coefficient list if a_d!=0, and otherwise use the constant list (1), which has no roots. This defines EVERY code, without partial decoding. Every nonzero finite integer coefficient list with last entry nonzero occurs: choose each u_k canonically as min{u:z(u)=a_k}, take tail t_{d+1}=0, encode backwards t_k=J(u_k,t_{k+1}), and use n=J(d,t_0). Finite backwards recursion has no arbitrary-index choice. By the local root-bound lemma each coded list has a finite root set of cardinality at most d. A finite subset of the ordered real field has a unique increasing root listing: its least element exists by lem-finite-subsets-listable (minimum consequence), and repeated deletion defines the rest; finite counting proves termination. This unique listing is specified from the root set, so forming all listings is Replacement by unique definition, NOT countable choice. For x in A let n(x)=min{n:x is a root of coded list n}, and let j(x) be its zero-based position in that list. Then x -> J(n(x),j(x)) is injective since equal pairs identify one entry in one uniquely ordered root list. Its image is a subset of N, hence at most countable by lem-subset-of-countable; the bijection onto its image transfers countability to A. A contains the embedded Q: if rational q has representative p/v with v!=0 then the nonzero coefficient list (-p,v) evaluates to zero at its embedded value by the rational/real field embedding laws. Thus the canonical injection N -> Q -> R lands in A. Combine that injection with A -> N using thm-schroder-bernstein, giving A approximately N, not just countable. Finally, if RA were countable, take the explicit bijection N -> A supplied by Schroder-Bernstein and one surjection N -> RA (handle the empty case separately), interleave on N^2 by the first coordinate 0 versus nonzero, then compose J inverse. This would make R countable, contradicting thm-r-uncountable. Only two existentially given enumerations are used, no countable-family choice or general countable-union theorem. The new example describes algebraicity locally from coefficient lists and does not consume later def-algebraic-element or polynomial-ring suppliers.
